messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change rolled yesterday (kernel v2.4 -> v2.5 selector), we've been seeing a 12-18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on the LLM-prod fleet. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/prefix-cache?range=24h

aj: can you post the metric names & a quick snippet of the query? seeing overall p99 latency creep too.

maya: metric is `prefix_cache.hitrate.v1` (per-model, per-region). Quick query: `sum(rate(prefix_cache_hitrate_total[5m])) / sum(rate(prefix_cache_requests_total[5m]))`. last 24h went from ~0.73 -> 0.60 on gpt-like-large. p50 token latency up ~6%.

sam: I ran a narrow repro — toggling the kernel selector back to v2.4 on a canary pool brings hit-rate back to ~0.71 within ~10 minutes (warmup). Suspect kernel change touches KV serialization or padding ordering.

elaine: important: in the rollout notes v2.5 added a new NVMemory layout optimization for attention keys to reduce mem copies. Could that change cache key bytes? cc @sam

sam: yup — v2.5 changed the LMKV layout (layer-major -> head-major) for on-device cache to optimize matmul memory access. If our cache key uses raw bytes of the KV blob (we do for speed) that will change the canonical key. That would explain whole-class cache misses.

aj: ohhhh. So clients see identical prompts but server-side binary differs -> miss. Any telemetry proving different key signatures?

maya: I pulled a small sample of cache keys and diffs. Example (base64 of first 24 bytes):
- v2.4: `Q2Fja0tleUJZVFNY...`
- v2.5: `Q2Fja0tleU...AAE=`
We also see many keys where only internal padding bytes differ.

sam: that's the smoking gun. We shouldn't use raw binary serialization for keying across kernel variants. Need a stable canonicalization layer (hash over logical KV fields).

elaine: agreed. But we also have SDKs/clients sending optional cache headers: `x-rw-cache-opt: prefer-cache|bypass` and `x-rw-cache-key-version`. Any chance clients set something unexpected?

maya: interestingly, the hit-rate drop is concentrated in customers using our older Python SDK (v0.8.*) that sets `x-rw-cache-key-version` implicitly to `auto` (we parse as binary). Newer SDKs send `x-rw-cache-key-version: v2` (canonicalized).

aj: reproduce steps I've been using locally:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "x-rw-cache-opt: prefer-cache" \
  -H "x-rw-client-id: test-canary" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-like-large","input":"Hello world"}' \
  https://api.redwood/v1/generate
```
Comparing responses between kernels gives same text but different cache-miss patterns.

sam: mitigation proposals:
1) Roll back kernel selector for prod pools -> immediate hit-rate recovery (fast).
2) Add canonicalization layer: compute canonical key = `sha256(model, prompt_id, seq_len, normalized_kv)` before storing/lookup (medium term).
3) Accept both key formats for a transitional window (read-path tries both) + emit `cache_key_format` telemetry (short term).

maya: +1 to 3 for minimal blast radius. We already emit `cache.lookup.key_format` in some telemetry but not everywhere.

elaine: can we add a header-based opt-in to force canonicalized keying from clients? e.g., `x-rw-cache-key-override: canonical-v1` so clients can opt into new behavior?

aj: that would help customers triage. Also need SDK fix to stop sending `auto` and set explicit version. Devex should publish a note.

devex-bot: @aj opened SDK ticket RW-9873: "python-sdk: set explicit cache key version header" — https://issues.redwood/RW-9873

sam: streaming edge cases: also noticed retries during streaming create duplicate partial prefix writes with slightly different KV order (because of race in the streaming encoder), leading to write thrash and lower hit-rate. We should gate streaming partial-writes behind idempotency keys.

maya: payload example of problematic header set from client (found in logs):
```
x-rw-cache-opt: prefer-cache
x-rw-cache-key-version: auto
x-rw-prefetch: true
x-rw-client-id: web-hero
```

aj: ops question: if we do read-path dual-format support, cost will go up (two lookups). Do we have data on how much extra latency that adds?

sam: microbenchmarks: local memtable lookup ~0.2ms, KV-store lookup ~3.5ms. Doing two lookups when the first misses adds ~3.5ms average. That's acceptable compared to current p50 token latency (~25ms) but will affect p99 tail a bit. We can limit dual-lookup to canary pools or set a sampling rate.

maya: action plan I propose:
- short (1): enable dual-format read on canary region + emit `cache_key_probe` event (today, 2h).
- short (2): push SDK patch to set explicit header + DevEx blog + telemetry updates (48h).
- med (3): implement canonicalization stable key and migrate writes (2 weeks).
- med (4): add streaming idempotency gate to partial prefix writes (1 week).
- fallback: rollback kernel selector if hit-rate doesn't recover (ASAP).

elaine: +1. Who owns the dual-read & telemetry? @sam for read-path, @aj for deployment, @maya for rollout verification.

aj: I'll prepare the canary rollout doc and quick feature flag. We'll use `ff.cache.dual_key_read` and limit to 5% fleet initially.

sam: I'll open a PR to implement fallback read and the `cache_key_probe` event (including sample payload: `{client, model, key_format_tried, hit}`) and add a small histogram for added latency.

maya: I'll run a differential hit-rate query and set an alert if canary doesn't show >=70% hit-rate within 30m of flag on.

devex-bot: @maya created doc: https://confluence.redwood/ops/cache-key-migration (private).

infra-bot: canary rollout started: `ff.cache.dual_key_read=5%` on region-us-east-1 at 2026-03-14T15:20:00Z.

aj: initial canary looks promising: +9% hit-rate in canary pool after 12m. Needs longer to stabilize.

sam: note for postmortem: add a test in kernel onboarding checklist — "does KV serialization change byte layout?" and ensure we bump cache key version when it does.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll update the incident / action tracker and loop in security for header semantics. If we see any customer escalations I'll ping @elaine. :pray:

elaine: thanks. one more: ensure we don't log raw KV bytes in telemetry. Use hashes only.

maya: agreed. will hash before logging.

aj: awesome. follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30.

sam: thanks, closing for now.
__comment: This file is a single Slack thread JSON for eng-runtime channel about kernel change causing prefix cache key mismatches and proposed mitigations.
